discipline: test.jsonl was written on Day 3, rebuilt blind on Day 4 when the splits were made payload-disjoint, and read for the first time here. Nothing was tuned after this ran.

sentr.note_on_recall: recall_pct = detected (any verdict but allow). neutralised_recall_pct = the payload does not reach the buying agent, because the listing was withheld or the span was sanitised out. The second is the one that describes what the agent is protected from; the gap between them is listings we flagged for review but still handed over.
sentr.note_on_flag: A flagged listing is sanitised and still sells. Only a BLOCKED listing earns nothing, so the blocked rate is the one that carries a rupee cost.
sentr.note_on_precision: Precision is prevalence-dependent and this split is 31% poisoned by construction, far above any real catalogue. Recall and FPR are the transferable numbers.

baseline.note_truncation: 2 listing(s) hit the 512-token limit and were read only in part. Sentr's classifier windows the full text instead, which is the point of chunking: on a long listing an unchunked detector never sees a payload written at the end.

corrections.what_happened: time.perf_counter() advanced about 10.6 hours during the baseline pass -- the laptop suspended mid-run, just after midnight. The recorded wall time of 38,501s is for a job that took roughly six minutes.
corrections.what_is_affected: Only these two timing fields. Recall, neutralised recall, precision, false-positive rates and every count are derived from verdicts, not from the clock, and are unaffected.
corrections.resolution: The numbers are left exactly as measured rather than edited, and this note records the fault. Baseline throughput should be cited from the Day 1 run (eval/results/day1_baseline_benign.json), which measured 3.4 listings/sec and p50 418ms over 6,000 real listings on the same hardware. eval/evaluate.py now cross-checks two clocks and withholds throughput rather than publishing a wrong figure.
corrections.not_a_rerun: The held-out set was NOT reopened to fix this. An instrumentation fault in a performance field does not justify a second look at test.jsonl.
